# Why a 50-problem single-source ladder after a broad course

The course has taught tools by idea. Codeforces now supplies a deliberately
ordered environment in which the statement is unfamiliar but the underlying
move should be recognizable. This is not a rating checklist: a 1400 can expose
an unlearned invariant more effectively than a rushed 2200.

Use [problem_sheet.pdf](problem_sheet.pdf) offline. It gives a concise original
restatement, the input/output contract, and a visible official URL for every
task. The linked Codeforces page is authoritative if a detail differs. Do not
open [editorial.pdf](editorial.pdf) until you have recorded an attempt.

# How to work one ladder problem

Give every attempt an evidence trail:

```text
first model | rejected model or counterexample | final invariant | test that changed my mind
```

For example, on `279B`, writing "try every start and extend" is not enough.
The useful record is:

```text
positive reading times -> a valid window stays valid after removing from left
invariant -> [left, right] is feasible after the while-loop
test -> one book longer than the full budget
```

That record explains why two pointers are valid and makes the same pattern
available on a different story.

## The 25-minute rule

For Gates 1 and 2, work alone for 25 focused minutes. If there is no model,
write the exact missing observation and read only the corresponding editorial
block. For Gates 3 and 4, use 40--60 minutes because modeling, not typing, is
usually the work. Do not replace an attempt with passive editorial reading.

After reading an editorial, close it and reproduce four things from memory:

1. the state or invariant;
2. the transition or greedy choice;
3. why a tempting alternative is wrong;
4. the asymptotic bound in the statement's variables.

# Gate 1: mechanical correctness

| Task | Course bridge | What must become automatic |
|---|---|---|
| 71A | Sections 1--2 | input loop, length boundary, exact output |
| 4C | Section 3 | a map whose value has a precise meaning |
| 363B | Sections 4--5 | fixed-window sum and first-index tie handling |
| 279B | Section 6 | a monotone two-pointer invariant |
| 158B | Sections 9--10 | greedy groups with a proof by forced partners |
| 706B | Section 8 | `upper_bound` / `bisect_right` as a counting query |

Do not race this gate. A wrong answer here should create a named regression
test: empty-looking edge cases are where conventions become habits.

# Gate 2: graph and DP modeling

| Task | Course bridge | Recognition question |
|---|---|---|
| 520B | Section 15 | what are the states and unit-cost moves? |
| 455A | Section 22 | what future conflict is summarized by one index? |
| 300C | Sections 29--32 | which digit sums can be constructed and counted? |
| 166B | Section 54 | how does a convex fan locate one polygon vertex? |
| 20C | Section 19 | are all edge weights nonnegative, and do I need a parent? |
| 161D | Section 26 | how many nodes at every bounded depth lie below me? |

For `161D`, use the bounded `k` from the statement to keep a depth-count DP at
each tree node. The ladder is ordered by dependency, not merely by rating.

# Gate 3: state compression and structures

| Task | Course bridge | Main danger |
|---|---|---|
| 580D | Section 27 | the last item is part of the DP state |
| 1245D | Section 18 | a virtual node turns stations into MST edges |
| 271D | Sections 43 and 55 | equality needs collision-aware substring identity |
| 61E | Section 36 | strict inequalities and duplicate values in Fenwick queries |
| 86D | Sections 40 and 42 | keep the current range statistic updated both ways |

At this gate, write a state table before coding. It should say what changes
when one item, vertex, character, or array endpoint is added and removed.

# Gate 4: reductions and advanced optimization

| Task | Course bridge | Reduction to state explicitly |
|---|---|---|
| 498C | Section 45 | prime-factor units, odd positions, even positions |
| 319C | Section 49 | each earlier DP state is a line queried at `a[i]` |

The hard part is often proving the reduction, not selecting a library template.
On `498C`, show why a unit of a prime cannot be used twice. On `319C`, derive
the line slope and intercept from the recurrence before choosing a hull.

# Gates 5--7: expert to red

Tasks 20--50 deliberately stop looking like one-technique exercises. They are
still ordered, but the order measures the amount of model compression, proof,
and engineering required rather than a single online rating number.

| Gate | Tasks | What changes in your attempt routine |
|---|---|---|
| 5 | 20--27 | derive a representation that turns many operations into logarithmic work |
| 6 | 28--40 | prove the reduction before choosing the advanced structure |
| 7 | 41--50 | derive the optimized recurrence or transformation from a slow oracle |

For Gates 5 and 6, spend at least 45 minutes before reading an editorial. For
Gate 7, first write a slow exact model and state precisely which monotonicity,
decomposition, or algebraic identity must justify the optimization. A correct
template with an unproved reduction is not a solved problem.

# A disciplined upsolve protocol

After a failed attempt, identify the earliest false sentence in your work:

| Failure | Repair exercise |
|---|---|
| wrong tool | list three statement signals and the competing tools |
| correct tool, wrong state | write two histories that reach the same old state but need different futures |
| proof gap | state the exchange, induction, or cut argument in three lines |
| implementation bug | preserve the smallest failing test and label the convention |
| complexity miss | count states and transitions independently |

Then solve a nearby task only after you can explain the repaired invariant
without looking. The editorial gives a route to understanding; it should not
become a substitute for retrieving the route yourself.

# Offline workflow

The sheet is intentionally concise enough to print. Before a travel day or an
offline session:

1. render this section with `make pdf`;
2. save `problem_sheet.pdf` and `editorial.pdf` locally;
3. hide the editorial until the attempt time ends;
4. once connected, submit through the visible Codeforces URL and compare any
   judge failure with the sheet's stated contract.

The URLs remain useful as references in a printed PDF even when they cannot be
clicked. They also avoid pretending that a course copy replaces the official
judge.

# Exercises

## A. Gate log

Solve the first four tasks without editorials. For each, write the invariant
and one smallest hostile test. Advance only when all four descriptions are
independent of the story wording.

## B. Model comparison

For `20C`, `1245D`, and `498C`, draw the graph used by the solution. Mark what
each node and edge means, then explain why every valid original choice maps to
one graph object and back.

## C. Compression audit

For `455A`, `580D`, `86D`, and `319C`, name precisely what information is kept
and what information is deliberately discarded. Give a counterexample showing
why discarding one more field would fail.

# Submission checklist

```text
[ ] I solved the offline restatement, not a remembered answer.
[ ] My notes contain a state/invariant and a disproof of one tempting approach.
[ ] The complexity counts the actual constrained quantity.
[ ] I preserved one test that would catch my original mistake.
[ ] I read the official linked statement before submitting.
```
